examples.ko: 큰 소리에 놀라 한 걸음 뒷걸음쳤어요.
examples.en: Startled by the loud noise, I stepped back one pace.
The child began to back away when he saw the dog.

examples.ko: 질문을 받자 그는 슬금슬금 뒷걸음쳐서 도망갔어요.
examples.en: When he was asked a question, he edged backward and slipped away.
As the economy worsens, sales are going backward.
Don't back down in the face of difficult tasks.

examples.ko: 뱀을 본 친구가 뒷걸음치며 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: My friend backed away and screamed when she saw a snake.

explain: '뒷걸음을 치다'를 붙여 쓴 말이에요. 뒤로 물러나는 동작뿐 아니라 '매출이 뒷걸음치다', '성적이 뒷걸음치다'처럼 숫자나 상황이 나빠질 때도 써요. 반대로 앞으로 나아가는 건 '앞으로 나아가다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I was startled to see a snake and backed away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒷걸음치다'와 뜻이 같고, '뒷걸음질'이 들어가서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 뒷걸음치다, and the 뒷걸음질 form is more commonly used.

phrases.en: It's dangerous, so everyone please step back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸을 뒤로 옮기라고 안내할 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy phrase for telling people to move back.

phrases.en: My grades have been slipping lately, and I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 걸음이 아니라 실력이나 숫자가 나빠졌다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use meaning ability or numbers got worse, not real walking.

explain_en: Step back out of fear or surprise, a physical reaction. It is a contracted form of '뒷걸음을 치다'. Besides physically stepping back, it is used when numbers or situations get worse, as in '매출이 뒷걸음치다' or '성적이 뒷걸음치다'. The opposite idea is '앞으로 나아가다' (to move forward).

t90.ax: Don't back down in the face of difficult tasks.

en: water and fire; (idiom) hardship, any difficulty

examples.ko: 그는 아들을 위해서라면 물불을 가리지 않아요.
examples.en: He will do anything at all for his son.

examples.ko: 돈을 벌려고 물불 안 가리고 일했어요.
examples.en: I worked with no thought for the hardship to earn money.

examples.ko: 물불도 안 가리는 사람이라 말리기 어려워요.
examples.en: He's a person who stops at nothing, so he's hard to stop.

examples.ko: 친구를 구하려고 물불 가리지 않고 뛰어갔어요.
examples.en: He ran off without a second thought to save his friend.
I applied everywhere, willing to do whatever it took to get a job.
If you charge in recklessly, you'll get badly hurt.

explain: 거의 '물불을 가리지 않다' 꼴로 나와요. 물이든 불이든 따지지 않는다는 뜻이라 위험이나 어려움을 신경 쓰지 않고 덤빌 때 써요. 가족이나 친구를 위해서면 헌신하는 느낌이고, 돈이나 이익을 위해서면 수단을 안 가린다는 비난으로 들려요.

phrases.example: 엄마는 아이 일이라면 물불을 가리지 않으세요.
phrases.en: My mom will do anything when it comes to her child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이든 불이든 따지지 않는다는 비유로, 위험이나 어려움을 신경 쓰지 않고 달려든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor of not caring whether it is water or fire; it means rushing in regardless of danger or difficulty.
phrases.en_equiv: go through fire and water; stop at nothing

explain_en: It almost always appears as '물불을 가리지 않다'. Water or fire makes no difference, so it is used for rushing in regardless of danger or difficulty. For family or friends it sounds devoted; for money or profit it sounds like using any means.

en: to be butted; to be gored

examples.en: A cow suddenly ran up, and a person got butted.
I almost got butted by a cow in a narrow alley.
I was butted by a goat and got a bruise on my arm.
The spot where I was hit still hurts.
Be careful that the child isn't butted by the cow.

examples.ko: 받히면 크게 다칠 수 있으니 멀리 떨어지세요.
examples.en: You can get badly hurt if you're butted, so stay far away.

explain: 소나 염소 같은 동물의 뿔이나 머리에 세게 부딪힐 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요. '바치다'와 발음이 같아서 글자를 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 차에 부딪힌 때는 보통 '치이다'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The child was butted by the goat's horns.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇에 받혔는지 말할 때 '에'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 에 to say what did the butting.

phrases.en: I was butted by a cow and hurt my leg.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받힌 결과로 다쳤다는 뜻을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to continue with the result of being hurt after being butted.
phrases.en_equiv: to get hurt by being butted

phrases.en: Be careful not to get butted when you are near cows.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심하라고 주의를 줄 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when warning someone to be careful.
phrases.en_equiv: to be careful not to be butted

explain_en: This is a passive form used when you are hit hard by an animal's horn or head, such as a cow's or goat's. It sounds the same as '바치다', so the spelling is easy to mix up. For being hit by a car, people more often say '치이다'.

en: to burn up; to set ablaze; to pour out (energy, passion)

examples.ko: 그는 마지막 경기에 모든 열정을 불살랐어요.
examples.en: He poured all his passion into the final match.

examples.ko: 옛날 편지를 모두 불살라 버리고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I wanted to burn all the old letters.

examples.ko: 젊은 시절 일에 청춘을 불사르며 살았어요.
examples.en: In my youth I lived pouring my whole youth into work.

examples.ko: 마지막 힘까지 불사르는 선수들의 모습이 감동적이었어요.
examples.en: It was moving to see the players give every last bit of strength.
Grandmother used to get rid of trash by burning it.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 이번 대회에 열정을 불살라요.
examples.en: Our team pours all its passion into this competition.

explain: 실제로 불에 태운다는 뜻으로도 쓰지만, '열정을 불사르다'처럼 마음과 힘을 다 쏟는다는 비유로도 자주 써요. '르' 불규칙이라 '불살라요, 불살랐어요'가 돼요. 일상에서 단순히 태울 때는 '태우다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 무대에서 모든 열정을 불살랐어요.
phrases.en: That athlete poured all of his passion into the stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음과 힘을 다 쏟는다는 비유로 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common figurative pairing, meaning to pour out all one's heart and energy.

phrases.example: 필요 없는 서류를 모두 불살라 버렸어요.
phrases.en: I burned up all the papers I didn't need.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 버리다'를 붙여 완전히 태워 없앤다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 버리다' gives the feel of burning something away completely.

phrases.en: He devoted his youth to research.
phrases.nuance_ko: 젊은 시절을 한 가지 일에 다 바쳤다는 뜻으로 글에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means giving one's youth entirely to one thing; common in writing.
phrases.en_equiv: to burn one's youth for something

explain_en: It can mean literally burning something, but it is also often used figuratively, as in '열정을 불사르다', for pouring all your heart and energy into something. It is a 르-irregular verb: '불살라요, 불살랐어요'. For simply burning something in daily life, people use '태우다'.

examples.ko: 아이가 잠든 사이에 살그머니 방을 나왔어요.
examples.en: I quietly left the room while the child was asleep.

examples.ko: 그는 내 옆으로 살그머니 다가와 앉았어요.
examples.en: He quietly came up next to me and sat down.
I opened the door carefully and peeked inside.
I was embarrassed, so I slipped my hand behind my back.

examples.ko: 수업 중에 살그머니 휴대폰을 꺼내 봤어요.
examples.en: I stealthily took out my phone during class.

examples.ko: 고양이가 살그머니 내 무릎 위로 올라왔어요.
examples.en: The cat softly climbed onto my lap.

explain: '살며시'와 비슷하게 소리 없이 조심스럽게 움직이는 느낌이에요. 남이 모르게 하는 행동에 잘 어울려요. '슬그머니'도 비슷하지만 눈치를 보며 슬쩍 하는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I closed the door quietly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살그머니'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 더 부드럽고 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '살그머니', but a bit softer and more common.

phrases.en: I quietly opened the door and came in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 나지 않게 조심해서 문을 열 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when opening a door carefully so it makes no noise.

phrases.en: He quietly took my hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 눈치채지 못하게 조심스럽게 하는 행동에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits actions done carefully without others noticing.

explain_en: Like '살며시', it describes moving quietly and carefully. It fits actions done without others noticing. '슬그머니' is similar, but it feels more like sneaking while watching people's reactions.

examples.en: At the back of the classroom, the kids are whispering about something.

examples.ko: 사람들이 내 얘기를 숙덕거리는 것 같아서 신경 쓰였어요.
examples.en: It seemed like people were whispering about me, and that bothered me.

examples.ko: 둘이서 숙덕거리지 말고 크게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't whisper between the two of you; say it out loud, please.

examples.ko: 이웃 사람들이 그 집 소문을 숙덕거렸어요.
examples.en: The neighbors whispered gossip about that family.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 숙덕거리던 직원들이 갑자기 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: The staff who had been whispering during the meeting suddenly went quiet.
Even if you whisper behind my back, I can hear everything.

explain: 남이 못 듣게 낮은 소리로 이야기한다는 느낌이고, 소문이나 험담처럼 부정적인 내용에 잘 어울려요. 비슷한 '수군거리다'도 같은 상황에서 쓰고, '쑥덕거리다'는 더 센 느낌의 말이에요.

phrases.en: People whisper behind my back.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숙덕거리다'와 비슷하게 낮은 소리로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '숙덕거리다', for talking in low voices.

phrases.en: It seems my friends are whispering behind my back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당사자가 없는 곳에서 몰래 이야기한다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feel of talking secretly where the person can't hear.

phrases.en: I can hear whispering in the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작게 속닥이는 소리를 명사처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the sound of low whispering.

explain_en: It suggests talking in a low voice so others can't hear, and fits negative content like rumors or gossip. '수군거리다' is used in similar situations, and '쑥덕거리다' is a stronger-sounding variant.

t90.ax: The neighbors whispered gossip about that family.

en: to be crushed; to be shattered

examples.en: I put the snacks in my bag and they ended up crushed.
Dry leaves crumble under my feet.
The cookie was crushed and only crumbs were left.
I gripped it hard and the paper cup in my hand got crushed.
I sprinkle crushed cookies over ice cream.

examples.ko: 상자가 눌려서 안에 있는 빵이 다 으스러질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The box got squashed and the bread inside almost got completely crushed.

explain: '부서지다'와 비슷하지만 눌리거나 짓눌려서 잘게 깨지는 느낌이 있어요. 힘을 주는 쪽에서 말할 때는 '으스러뜨리다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The child crushed the dry leaves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘을 주는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the subject is the person applying the force.

phrases.en: I hugged my friend so tightly it felt like crushing, since we hadn't met in a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 세게 껴안는 모습을 과장해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say, with some exaggeration, that you hugged very tightly.
phrases.en_equiv: to hug so hard it feels like crushing

phrases.en: These cookies are fragile and get crushed easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금만 눌러도 잘게 깨지는 물건에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for things that break into small pieces with just a little pressure.

explain_en: Brittle or hard things break under pressure (으스러진 과자) It is similar to '부서지다' but suggests something breaking into small pieces from being pressed or squashed. When you focus on the one applying force, the word is '으스러뜨리다'.

t90.ax: Dry leaves crumble under my feet.

examples.en: Nobody will do you any harm.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 나중에 해코지할까 봐 무서워요.
examples.en: I'm afraid that person might try to harm me later.

examples.ko: 누가 제 자전거에 해코지를 했나 봐요.
examples.en: Someone seems to have tampered with my bike out of spite.
I couldn't speak up because I feared retaliation.

examples.ko: 그 개는 사람에게 해코지는 안 하니까 걱정 마세요.
examples.en: That dog doesn't hurt people, so don't worry.

examples.ko: 해코지 같은 짓은 절대 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Never do anything spiteful like that.

explain: 남에게 몰래 또는 일부러 해를 끼치는 짓을 말해요. 대개 '해코지하다', '해코지를 당하다'처럼 쓰고, 말로 할 때 자주 나오는 구어적인 말이에요. 앙갚음하려는 나쁜 마음이 느껴져요.

phrases.example: 혼자 있으면 해코지를 당할까 봐 걱정돼요.
phrases.en: I'm worried I'll be harmed if I'm alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해를 입는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the person who suffers the harm.
phrases.en_equiv: to be harmed out of spite

phrases.en: I heard that person secretly did something nasty to them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해코지하다'와 같은 뜻이고, 일부러 해를 끼친 쪽을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same as 해코지하다; used for the one who deliberately causes harm.

phrases.en: People who secretly do harm to others are really cowardly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몰래'가 붙으면 숨어서 나쁜 짓을 하는 모습이 더 잘 드러나요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 몰래 ('secretly') highlights the hidden, sneaky nature of the act.

explain_en: Deliberate harm to a person out of spite, colloquial. It means deliberately or secretly causing someone harm. It is usually used as '해코지하다' or '해코지를 당하다' and is a fairly colloquial word. It carries a sense of malicious intent, like payback.

t90.ax: Nobody will do you any harm.

en: to become short of breath; to be out of breath

examples.en: I ran up the stairs and got out of breath.
When I get nervous, my breathing gets faster.
If you get short of breath, take a short rest before going on.

examples.ko: 달리기를 하다 보니 숨이 점점 가빠지기 시작했어요.
examples.en: As I kept running, my breathing began to get heavier.

examples.ko: 가슴이 답답하고 숨이 가빠져서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My chest felt tight and I was short of breath, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 발표 때 갑자기 말이 빨라지고 숨이 가빠질까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I worry that during the presentation I will suddenly talk fast and get short of breath.

explain: 주로 '숨이 가빠지다, 호흡이 가빠지다'의 모양으로 써요. 이미 숨이 찬 상태는 '숨이 가쁘다'이고, 가빠지다는 점점 그렇게 변해 간다는 느낌이에요. 'ㅡ'가 빠져서 '가빠요, 가빠졌어요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: I ran, so my breathing is getting short.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가빠지다'의 해요체로, 점점 숨이 차는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form, with the feeling of breathing getting harder step by step.

phrases.en: If I walk slowly, I don't get out of breath.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨이 차지 않는다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative, meaning you stay comfortable.
phrases.en_equiv: does not get out of breath

phrases.en: I just ran, so I'm out of breath.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 숨이 찬 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of already being out of breath.

explain_en: It mostly appears as '숨이 가빠지다' or '호흡이 가빠지다'. '숨이 가쁘다' describes the state of already being out of breath, while this word means gradually getting into that state. The ㅡ drops out, giving '가빠요' and '가빠졌어요'.

examples.en: The mask strap rubs against the back of my ears and hurts.
A mosquito bit the back of my ear and it keeps itching.
My glasses are small, so the backs of my ears hurt.
It was so cold that even the backs of my ears turned red.
At the beach, only the backs of my ears got sunburned.

examples.ko: 제 말을 귓등으로 듣지 말고 잘 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't brush off what I say and listen carefully.

explain: 몸의 부위로 쓸 때는 안경다리나 마스크 끈이 닿는 귀 쪽을 말해요. '귓등으로 듣다'라는 표현으로도 나와요.

phrases.example: 선생님 말씀을 귓등으로 듣다가 숙제를 놓쳤어요.
phrases.en: I half-listened to the teacher and missed the homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣기는 해도 마음에 담지 않고 흘려듣는다는 뜻이라 비난하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means hearing something without taking it in, and carries a tone of criticism.
phrases.en_equiv: let it go in one ear and out the other

explain_en: As a body part it refers to the area of the ear where glasses arms or mask straps rest. It also appears in the expression '귓등으로 듣다'.

examples.en: Grandfather wore a magoja over his hanbok.
On Seollal, my father wore a vest and a magoja.
The magoja has pretty buttons on it.
A magoja is nice with winter hanbok because it's warm.
Wearing a magoja, you look dignified.

examples.ko: 저고리 위에 마고자를 하나 더 입었어요.
examples.en: I put on a magoja over the jeogori as one more layer.

explain: 남자 한복에서 저고리 위에 덧입는 겉옷이에요. 조끼, 두루마기와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 마고자는 깃이 없고 앞에 단추를 달아 입는 옷이에요. 명절이나 결혼식 같은 날에 한복을 입을 때 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: On New Year's Day my grandfather wore a magoja.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입는다고 할 때 '입다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '입다' for wearing the garment.

phrases.en: A hanbok magoja is warm, so it's good in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한복과 함께 입는 옷이라는 것을 보여 주는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows that it is worn together with hanbok.

phrases.en: A button came off my magoja, so I sewed it back on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마고자는 앞에 단추를 달아 입어서 이 말을 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A magoja has buttons in front, so this phrase is common.

explain_en: It is an outer layer worn over the jeogori in men's hanbok. It is easy to confuse with the vest or the durumagi, but the magoja has no collar and fastens with buttons at the front. You see it when people wear hanbok on holidays or at weddings.

examples.en: I'm so cold that my whole body is shivering.

examples.ko: 강아지가 천둥 소리에 바들바들 떨고 있어요.
examples.en: The puppy is trembling at the sound of thunder.
My hands were shaking before the presentation.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 지팡이를 잡은 손을 바들바들 떠세요.
examples.en: My grandfather's hand holding the cane is trembling.

examples.ko: 겁이 나서 다리가 바들바들 떨려 못 걸었어요.
examples.en: I was so scared that my legs shook and I couldn't walk.

examples.ko: 바들바들 떨지 말고 심호흡을 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't shake like that, try taking a deep breath.

explain: 주로 '떨다, 떨리다'와 함께 써요. '벌벌'이 더 널리 쓰이고, '바들바들'은 작고 가늘게 계속 떠는 느낌이에요. 추위, 무서움, 긴장, 힘이 없을 때 모두 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I took the test paper with trembling hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 일부를 작고 가늘게 계속 떠는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a part of the body trembling in a small, continuous way.

phrases.en: I'm so scared that my legs are shaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 떠는 게 아니라 저절로 몸이 떨리는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the body shaking on its own, not by choice.

phrases.en: I trembled with fear.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바들바들'보다 더 널리 쓰이고 큰 떨림에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More widely used than 바들바들, and fits bigger trembling too.

explain_en: It mostly goes with '떨다' or '떨리다'. '벌벌' is more widely used, while '바들바들' suggests small, thin, continuous trembling. It fits cold, fear, nerves or weakness.

t90.ax: I'm so cold that my whole body is shivering.

en: to stagger; to totter; to walk weakly

examples.ko: 너무 지쳐서 그는 비척거리며 집에 들어왔어요.
examples.en: He was so exhausted that he staggered into the house.

examples.ko: 오래 아픈 할머니가 비척거리면서 방을 나오셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother, who has been ill for a long time, came out of her room tottering.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 갑자기 비척거려서 제가 팔을 잡았어요.
examples.en: He suddenly staggered, so I grabbed his arm.

examples.ko: 산에서 내려오는 길에 다리가 풀려 비척거렸어요.
examples.en: My legs gave way on the way down the mountain and I stumbled along.
Why are you wobbling like that? Are you sick?

examples.ko: 비척거리지 말고 여기 앉아서 좀 쉬세요.
examples.en: Don't totter around; sit here and rest a bit.

explain: '비틀거리다', '휘청거리다'와 비슷하지만, 힘이 없거나 몸이 안 좋아서 제대로 걷지 못하는 느낌이 강해요. 대화에서는 '비틀거리다'로 바꿔 말해도 돼요. '비척대다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: Grandfather is staggering as he walks over.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비척거리다'와 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 비척거리다 and interchangeable.

phrases.en: I was so sleepy that I stumbled around.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서 더 흔한 말로 균형을 잃고 흔들릴 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in conversation, and also used when losing balance.

phrases.en: He was exhausted and walked unsteadily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘없이 휘청이며 걷는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes walking in a weak, swaying way.

explain_en: It is similar to '비틀거리다' and '휘청거리다', but it strongly suggests someone too weak or unwell to walk properly. In conversation you can swap in '비틀거리다'. '비척대다' means the same thing.

en: to pout; to purse one's lips; to protrude lips

examples.en: The child is holding back tears, pushing out his lips.

examples.ko: 기분이 상했는지 동생이 계속 입을 삐죽거려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling keeps pouting, probably upset.
Don't pout, say it in words.
It was cute to see my friend pouting.
She pouted because she didn't get praised.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 서운하면 삐죽거려서 금방 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: When that child feels hurt she pouts, so it's easy to tell.

explain: 서운하거나 울음이 날 때 입술을 내미는 동작이에요. '입을 삐죽거리다'처럼 자주 쓰고, 같은 뜻으로 '삐죽이다'나 '삐죽대다'도 있어요.

phrases.en: The child turned away, pouting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 다른 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An alternative form with the same meaning.

phrases.en: My younger sibling seems upset and is pouting.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-대다'를 붙여 같은 동작이 계속되는 느낌을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-daeda' conveys the action continuing.

phrases.en: I was angry and stuck out my lips.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입을 한 번 내미는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for pushing out the lips once.

explain_en: It is the movement of pushing out the lips when feeling hurt or about to cry, often as '입을 삐죽거리다'. '삐죽이다' and '삐죽대다' also exist with the same meaning.

t90.ax: Don't pout, say it in words.

examples.en: I fell and got a scratch on my knee.
Please put ointment on the scratch.
I went through a thorn bush and my legs are covered in scratches.

examples.ko: 작은 생채기라도 소독은 꼭 해야 해요.
examples.en: Even a small scratch needs to be disinfected.

examples.ko: 친구의 말 한마디가 마음에 생채기를 냈어요.
examples.en: One word from my friend left a scratch on my heart.
A scratch mark remained on the child's face.

explain: '상처'보다 작고 가벼운, 긁히거나 할퀸 상처에 써요. '마음의 생채기'처럼 사소해 보여도 아픈 마음의 상처를 비유할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I got a scratch on my arm from the cat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상처가 저절로 생겼을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for a scratch that appears on its own.

phrases.en: I accidentally scratched my arm with my fingernail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 또는 무엇이 일부러나 실수로 상처를 만들었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone or something causes the scratch.

phrases.example: 그 말이 제 마음에 생채기를 남겼어요.
phrases.en: Those words left a scratch on my heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작아 보여도 아픈 마음의 상처를 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor for an emotional hurt that seems small but stings.

explain_en: It is smaller and lighter than '상처' (wound), used for a scrape or a claw mark. It is also used figuratively, as in '마음의 생채기', for a hurt that looks small but still stings.

t90.ax: Please put ointment on the scratch.
